chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who circles between Safa and Marwah, does he rest? He said, 'Yes, if he wishes, he sits on Safa and on Marwah and between them, so he sits.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa (the hill from which Sa'i begins)
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: and Marwah (the hill where Sa'i ends)
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: he circles/walks (referring to the ritual of Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sit and rest while performing Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Sa'i ritual, confirming that resting is not only permissible but can be done specifically on the Safa and Marwah structures or anywhere in between. This ruling alleviates the physical burden on pilgrims, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*yusr*) in worship, as opposed to rigid asceticism. The hadith underscores that the ritual's essence is the act of moving between the two points, allowing for pauses to accommodate individual capacity.
